Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
935 PM EDT Tue Aug 4 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Nothing.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Monitoring potential for localized urban flooding tonight
  into Wednesday morning as a warm front lifts north.

- 2) Daily shower and thunderstorm chances are expected from
  Wednesday into early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Monitoring potential for localized urban flooding 
tonight into Wednesday morning as a warm front lifts north.

18Z deterministic guidance have shifted axis of heaviest
rainfall westward overnight to the Rt 15 corridor. Still have 
low confidence on placement of heaviest rainfall and whether 
there will be sufficient rainfall to cause any flooding.

Previous afd...

Looking a bit more closely at the threat for overnight heavy
rainfall, the 12Z high-resolution models are not showing the
strongest of signals. However, there are a number of
meteorological conditions which warrant this situation to bear
watching. This includes: (1) Precipitable water values (PWAT) 
increasing from 1.50 to around 2 to 2.25 inches, (2) An uptick 
in warm advection with the approaching front, and (3) Enhanced 
lift with vorticity swinging northward from an upper low across 
the Mid-South. Where the heavy rainfall sets up will dictate the
degree of impact. If this impacts the urban sprawl around the 
D.C. metro, poor drainage will support a risk of flash flooding.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Daily shower and thunderstorm chances are
expected Wednesday into early next week.

In the wake of what morning convection materializes, the models
do show a brief lull in the action. The northward pushing warm
front eventually stalls nearby before shearing out. Likewise,
the upper low across the Mid-South region begins to fill
although the reflection of this circulation still shows up
across southern West Virginia on Wednesday. Remaining
perturbations around this mid/upper low should help fire off
some afternoon/evening thunderstorms. A number of models depict
anomalous moisture lingering across the region with PWATs over 2
inches for those of the Blue Ridge. While no clear signal
exists, slow moving cells could produce a few instances of flash
flooding. However, the longstanding drought conditions could
easily curb that threat.

Seasonably warm temperatures and typical early August humidity
remain a fixture in the forecast for the foreseeable future. A
broad subtropical ridge in the mid/upper levels will continue
retrograding from the western Atlantic back toward the Eastern
Seaboard. At the same time, while the strongest jet energy
remains tied to the northern tier states, the quasi-zonal flow
aloft will steer a myriad from weak to modest shortwaves toward
the northeastern U.S. As usual, these types of features are of
low confidence given the mesoscale nature of the convective 
elements. As such, will continue to maintain a risk of strong to
severe thunderstorms as well as isolated instances of flash 
flooding each day. At this point, Friday presents the most 
active looking day of the period. However, this could easily 
change as global models continue to waver from run to run.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...

VFR conditions continue through the evening and early overnight
hours. This is accompanied by mainly light easterly winds. 
However, lowering ceilings will support restrictions across all 
terminals tonight into Wednesday morning. Locally heavier 
rainfall could impact the D.C. metro area terminals. Some 
improvements are expected by midday before another round of 
storms could impact the area. PROB30 groups accompany this 
threat, particularly in the 20Z-00Z window on Wednesday.

Winds shift to mainly south to southwesterly for the foreseeable
future as a Bermuda high pressure system persists across the 
western Atlantic. Daily convective chances each afternoon and 
evening will support convective-driven restrictions. With little
change in the upcoming pattern, this sort of forecast will 
likely hold for the next several days.

&&

.MARINE...
While today largely presents tranquil weather across the
waterways, this will change for the mid to late week period.
Diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms should increase the
risk of hazardous conditions for boaters and swimmers. Special
Marine Warnings would accompany any of the stronger storms, with
any cell capable of producing frequent lightning and gusty
winds. In terms of gradient winds, a few periods of southerly
channeling may warrant some short-fused Small Craft Advisories.
Most notably, this would include Wednesday evening into
Thursday, as well as Friday evening into the night.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies continue to remain on the lower end as northeast
to easterly winds persist. Southerly winds will return tonight 
behind a warm front that lifts north through the area. Anomalies
climb again mid to late week in response to return southerly 
flow. Additional periods of coastal flooding are possible at 
times of high tide at sensitive locations.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...Flood Watch from 4 AM EDT Wednesday through Wednesday morning 
     for DCZ001.
MD...Flood Watch from 4 AM EDT Wednesday through Wednesday morning 
     for MDZ013-016-504.
VA...Flood Watch from 4 AM EDT Wednesday through Wednesday morning 
     for VAZ053>056-502-527.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$
